# Copilot Instructions for AI Coding Agents

## Project Overview
This repository contains documentation for Laravel, structured as a collection of Markdown files. Each file covers a specific topic or component of the Laravel framework. There is no application code—this is a documentation-only project.

## Structure & Conventions
- Each major Laravel topic is documented in its own `.md` file at the root of the repository (e.g., `routing.md`, `eloquent.md`, `validation.md`).
- Files are named using lowercase, hyphen-separated words matching the topic name.
- There are no subdirectories for documentation content; all files are at the top level.
- No code samples are executed or tested—this is a static documentation set.

## Editing & Contribution Patterns
- When updating documentation, keep explanations concise and focused on Laravel best practices.
- Use code blocks for PHP, Blade, or CLI examples. Prefer real-world, idiomatic Laravel usage.
- Maintain consistent formatting: use headings, lists, and code blocks as seen in existing files.
- Cross-reference related topics by linking to other Markdown files (e.g., `[See: routing.md]`).
- Do not introduce application logic, scripts, or build/test workflows—this repo is for documentation only.

## Special Notes for AI Agents
- Do not add, remove, or rename documentation files unless explicitly instructed.
- Do not generate or update code outside of Markdown documentation.
- If unsure about Laravel conventions, refer to the official [Laravel documentation](https://laravel.com/docs) for examples.
- When in doubt, match the style and structure of existing Markdown files.

## Key Files
- All documentation: `*.md` at the repository root
- This guide: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

---
For questions about documentation style or Laravel conventions, consult the official Laravel docs or ask for clarification in a pull request.
